value.answer: For short-term use at low doses (around 5 mg or less), it looks fine for most adults. Side effects are usually mild, like headache or grogginess, and they fade when you stop. Long-term safety is less clear. A preliminary study presented in November 2025 linked 12+ months of use with higher heart failure risk, but it isn't peer-reviewed and can't prove cause, and a later analysis found no link (I only saw a summary of that one). Some experts say not to use it long-term without a good reason. Supplement strength also varies a lot, and it can interact with blood thinners and antidepressants, so check with a doctor or pharmacist if you take either.
